_comment: outcome.kind 'alert'            -> DemoBlaze correctly refuses the order.
outcome.kind 'purchaseAccepted' -> DemoBlaze takes the order when it should not.
The second kind records a real product defect. The assertion matches what the
application actually does, so the suite stays green for a bug it did not cause,
while the defect id keeps it visible. See the defect log in README.md.
Expiry dates are tokens expanded at run time by utils/dates.ts. '{{year-5}}'
keeps the malformed-card row meaning 'an expiry year in the past' forever,
which a literal 1999 would eventually stop demonstrating clearly.

cases.title: refuses an order when the checkout form is empty

outcome.message: Please fill out Name and Creditcard.

cases.title: refuses an order with a name but no credit card

outcome.message: Please fill out Name and Creditcard.

cases.title: refuses an order with a credit card but no name

outcome.message: Please fill out Name and Creditcard.

cases.title: accepts a malformed credit card, expiry month and expiry year

outcome.shouldHaveBeen: The order should be refused: the card is not numeric, month 13 does not exist and the expiry year is five years in the past. purchaseOrder() checks only that name and card are non-empty.

cases.title: accepts an order placed with an empty cart

outcome.shouldHaveBeen: Place Order should be unavailable, or the order refused, when the cart holds no items.

cases.title: accepts an order with no address and no expiry date

outcome.shouldHaveBeen: The order should be refused, or the expiry date at least required: country, city, month and year were all left blank and the order was still taken. purchaseOrder() validates name and card only, so the other four fields are decorative -- an order is accepted with nowhere to ship it and no expiry to authorise the card against.
